note: an ordinary session id is left exactly alone
the whole allowed set passes through: letters, digits, . _ -
only a leading DOT is guarded; a leading dash is an ordinary id
empty must still name a file
an id that strips to nothing must still name a file
the parent directory itself: dots survive the strip, the guard covers them
the attack this exists for: no separator survives, so it cannot escape the spool
an absolute path becomes one relative component
traversal in the middle: dots are harmless without separators
percent-encoded separators are not decoded, and % is not in the allow-list
backslash is a separator on some hosts and is not in the allow-list either
a dotfile is not the collector's to create
non-ASCII is stripped whole, byte-wise or char-wise alike
a multi-byte character inside an otherwise fine id takes no ASCII with it
idempotent: sanitizing an already-sanitized id changes nothing
